subject: ClearHealth: request for uptime apportionment and credit after 11/15 partial degradation
messages:
From: Avery Collins <avery.collins@clearhealth.com>
To: naomi.feldman@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 16:04:00 -0800
Subject: Partial outage 11/15 — request for credit (inbound probes show 12m)

Hi Naomi,

We detected a customer-impacting interruption to ClearHealth API traffic on 2027-11-15 between 15:22 and 15:34 PST (12 minutes) — several of our production callers returned 5xx or timed out. Our external probe network and application logs are attached (clearhealth_probe_log_20271115.json).

ClearHealth depends on the Redwood hosted inference API for tokenization and reranking in our ingest path; this incident caused a multi-tenant timeout cascade and impacted scheduled patient-data imports. Please confirm:

- What portion of our 12m outage is attributable to Redwood?
- Are third-party provider maintenance windows counted in Redwood uptime?
- Requesting full SLA credit if the service is counted as unavailable for the full interval.

We need a formal apportionment and a timeline we can share with compliance.

Thanks,
Avery Collins
Director of Platform Engineering
ClearHealth

From: naomi.feldman@redwood.com
To: Avery Collins <avery.collins@clearhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 16:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Partial outage 11/15 — request for credit (inbound probes show 12m)

Hi Avery — thanks for the heads up and the probe logs. I've looped in Marissa (CS) and Ben (Escalations) so we can triage quickly and get you an apportionment.

Immediate steps:
- Our infra team will pull the ingress/egress traces and peer exchanges for 15:15–15:45 PST.
- We'll compare our request-level error counts and KV cache stats to your traces.
- Expect a preliminary technical note and proposed credit by tomorrow morning.

Can you also send a representative application trace (stack traces + timing) for a failing request? I saw trace-sample-11-15.txt attached, that will help.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com
(415) 555-0189

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: naomi.feldman@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 16 Nov 2027 08:12:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Partial outage 11/15 — initial infra analysis

Quick summary of infra findings (preliminary):
- At 2027-11-15 15:20:30 PST we observed an increase in 5xx responses on the edge for the ClearHealth tenant.
- Upstream peer (EdgeX CDN provider) reported an emergency maintenance window starting 15:18 PST that caused a flapping peering session for ~9 minutes. Their status page: https://status.edgex.example/incident/311.
- Our origin instances experienced two short periods of degraded request processing: 15:23:00–15:27:00 (4 minutes) and 15:33:30–15:34:15 (45 seconds).
- Between 15:27 and 15:33 most requests were successful; the client-side probe gap (15:22–15:34) maps to both the CDN flapping and the short origin slowdown.

Prelim apportionment (by observed network/processing impact):
- Attributable to EdgeX third-party peering: ~7 minutes (their session flap + downstream queuing).
- Attributable to Redwood origin processing/queueing: ~4 minutes (15:23–15:27).

Notes on SLA: Redwood's standard uptime policy excludes third-party carrier/provider interruptions unless our telemetry shows no impact to our front-door (for example, if our edge fully served requests via alternate paths). Given the mixed signal, I recommend we treat this as a mixed attribution.

I'll attach the raw request-timeline extract and a CSV with the minute-by-minute event map (uploaded to the Drive link).

—Marcus
Senior Site Reliability Engineer
marcus_lin@redwood.com

From: Avery Collins <avery.collins@clearhealth.com>
To: naomi.feldman@redwood.com
Cc: ops@clearhealth.com
Date: Tue, 16 Nov 2027 09:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Partial outage 11/15 — initial infra analysis

Naomi / team — thanks for the quick analysis. ClearHealth appreciates the breakdown, but we disagree with the apportionment. From our standpoint, the customer experience was a continuous 12-minute failure window — our retries and fallbacks were exhausted. We also saw error spikes across multiple regions, not just traffic routed through EdgeX.

We need Redwood to:
- Provide the full audit logs showing request-level routing decisions for 15:15–15:40.
- Reconsider crediting the full 12 minutes, because third-party flaps are still within Redwood's delivery surface and we pay for end-to-end availability.

If we can't reach an agreement by EOW, we will escalate to procurement/legal and request a formal SLA claim.

Avery

From: naomi.feldman@redwood.com
To: Avery Collins <avery.collins@clearhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 16 Nov 2027 11:23:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Partial outage 11/15 — proposed compromise and next steps

Hi Avery — thanks for the clear ask and for the additional traces. We want to be fair and minimize friction. Proposed path forward: 

1) Full audit bundle: we'll provide per-request routing logs and hop-level latencies for 15:15–15:40 PST (link in related_links). Expect S3 delivery by 17:00 PST today.
2) Credit proposal: apportionment-based credit equal to 66% of the 12-minute window (i.e., 8 minutes) applied to your next invoice. Rationale: 4m clearly attributable to Redwood origin; remaining minutes predominantly due to EdgeX peering.
3) Optional: If ClearHealth prefers a simpler outcome, we can grant a goodwill credit for the full 12 minutes (one-time), outside standard SLA rules, in exchange for a short post-incident postmortem call and a commitment to keep the incident private for 30 days while we complete vendor remediation.

Please confirm which option you prefer (apportioned credit vs. one-time goodwill full credit) and whether you want the full audit bundle. If you choose the goodwill route we will route approval through leadership and can confirm by EOD.

Regards,
Naomi Feldman
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com
(415) 555-0189

Attachments: redwood_sla_apportionment_20271116.csv (breakdown), trace-sample-11-15.txt (customer sample)
